### Observed differences

- Case entry shifted: in the later window, A01 appears in about 50 of every 100 cases, down from about 58, while A02 and A03 each appear in about 50 of every 100, up from about 43 (115 → 101 and 85 → 99 of 200 traces). Roughly 7 in 100 cases moved from A01-involving runs to runs containing A02/A03. [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003]
- In the later window, the loop around A04 runs more often: A04's mean occurrences rise from about 1.6 to 2.1 per trace (repeats in about 34% → 38% of traces) and its presence from about 43 to 50 of every 100 cases; A11 rises from about 0.8 to 1.0 occurrences per trace (repeats in about 15% → 21% of traces) and A12 from about 0.8 to 1.0. [OCC004, OCC011, OCC012]
- The consecutive group A05, A07, A09, A10 is traversed more often per case in the later window, although its presence per case stays flat at about 23 of every 100 cases: each of the four rises from about 0.4 to 0.5 mean occurrences per trace, with repeats in about 11% → 13% of traces. [OCC005, OCC007, OCC009, OCC010]
- Successor choices within that group flipped in the later window: A05 now favours A10 over A07 (54% vs 41%, previously 43% vs 49%), A10 now favours A07 over A09 (50% vs 43%, previously 41% vs 53%), A07 now favours A09 over A10 (53% vs 40%, previously 45% vs 48%), and A09 returns to A04 in 99% of its outgoing transitions (95% before) while its loop back to A05 shrinks from 5% to 1%. [DIR003, DIR004, DIR005, DIR006]
- Smaller movements in the later window: A06 is present in about 28 of every 100 cases (up from about 23) and A08 in about 22 (up from about 20, unremarkable against random re-splits); A04's split between A11 and A12 stays near even (48/52 → 51/49) and A02 still leads almost exclusively to A04 (100% → 97%). [OCC006, OCC008, DIR002, DIR001]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the possibility that the cyclic core around A04 is executed more often in the later window. This core consists of the A04–A11/A12 loop (A04 passes on to A11 or A12 in near-equal shares, and A11 returns to A04 almost always) together with the sequence A05, A07, A09, A10 that feeds back into A04. Every activity in this core occurs more times per case than before (A04 about 1.6 → 2.1; A11 and A12 about 0.8 → 1.0; A05/A07/A09/A10 about 0.4 → 0.5), more traces contain repeats (for example A11: 15% → 21%), and entry into the core increased, with about 7 in 100 cases shifting from A01-involving runs to A02/A03-involving runs while A02 leads almost exclusively to A04 in both windows. The increases are consistent in direction across the whole core — the four sequence activities show identical profiles (each present in 45 → 46 traces), so their items reflect one behaviour rather than four independent confirmations — and the occurrence increases and the entry shift each exceed about 80% of random re-splits of the pooled data. Limitations: each window holds only 200 traces; no screening baseline was provided, so the number of findings expected by chance under no change could not be checked; and the evidence cannot show whether the extra repetitions come from the additional entering cases or from more iterations within existing ones. [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, OCC004, OCC005, OCC007, OCC009, OCC010, OCC011, OCC012, DIR001, DIR002, DIR007]

Other differences: within the A05/A07/A09/A10 sequence the preferred successors flipped as described above, which is consistent with A07 and A10 exchanging their usual positions (towards A05 → A10 → A07 → A09 in the later window, from A05 → A07 → A10 → A09 before); this ordering change is not part of the repetition hypothesis, and because only successor shares are available (no direct order-relational items), the exchange reading remains an interpretation. A06 also appears somewhat more often (about 23 → 28 of every 100 cases). [DIR003, DIR004, DIR005, DIR006, OCC006]

An important competing explanation the evidence cannot rule out is sampling variation: with 200 traces per window, smaller shifts such as A08's rise, A04's slight rebalance between A11 and A12, or the small reshuffle of A12's outgoing transitions fall within the range random re-splits produce (empirical strengths about 0.04–0.52), so parts of the overall pattern could be noise rather than one underlying change. [OCC008, DIR002, DIR008]
